# AI Context Bootstrap — READ FIRST

> **Canonical guidance for all AIs (ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) working on _kg-automation_.**

## Operate GitHub-first
- **System of record:** GitHub `kentonium3/kg-automation`.
- **Read context** from Dropbox if you're on a host with Dropbox installed; **never edit** in Dropbox.
- **Edit / generate** only in a Git working copy (feature branches) or in a dev container/Codespace.
- **Use Handoff Runner** for file creation/edits via JSON requests in `ai-agents/shared/handoffs/`.

## Handoff Runner — how to use
1) Create a feature branch.
2) Add `*-chatgpt-to-handoff-runner-request.json` under `ai-agents/shared/handoffs/` describing file edits.
3) Run **Actions → Handoff Runner** using that branch.
4) Open PR → wait for **Docs CI / validate** → merge.

**Guards:** runner is deny-listed from `.github/workflows/**` and won’t push to `main`.

## Claude Code / dev container
- Open folder → Dev Containers: “Open in Container” (provided in `.devcontainer/`).
- VS Code tasks:
  - `docs: validate`
  - `docs: build registries`
  - `docs: render docgraph`

## When unsure about paths
- See `docs/handbooks/eci-path-resolution.md`.

## Core handbooks
- Handoff Runner: `docs/handbooks/handoff-runner.md`
- Agent Handbook (pre-PR checklist): `docs/handbooks/agent-handbook.md`
- Docs review cadence: `docs/handbooks/docs-review-operating-model.md`
- Local Worker: `docs/handbooks/local-worker.md`

# Handoff Runner — How to Use

**Purpose:** Safely apply file edits via JSON handoffs on a feature branch. Validates with Docs CI before merge.

## Flow
1. Create feature branch.
2. Add JSON request under `ai-agents/shared/handoffs/`.
3. Run **Actions → Handoff Runner** with that branch.
4. Runner writes files + a `*-github-runner-response.json`.
5. Open PR → Docs CI must pass → merge.

## Guarantees & guards
- **No commits to `main`** (workflow guard).
- **Workflow edits deny-listed**: runner refuses `.github/workflows/**` unless an explicit allow flag is set (human change preferred).
- Responses are committed to the **same branch**.

## JSON request shape
```json
{
  "type":"handoff.request",
  "handoff_id":"1234",
  "from_agent":"chatgpt",
  "to_agent":"handoff-runner",
  "purpose":"What will change",
  "inputs":{"file_edits":[{"path":"docs/x.md","content":"..."}]}
}
```

## When to use Local Worker instead
- Needs host apps, LAN, or Dropbox-local checks. See `./local-worker.md`.

# Agent Handbook — Pre-PR Checklist

Use this before opening any PR:

- [ ] Changes created through **Handoff Runner** on a feature branch (not `main`).
- [ ] Markdown has YAML front-matter (`id/title/doc_type/status/owners/last_validated`).
- [ ] New docs linked from bootstrap / handbooks.
- [ ] Relative links resolve (run `docs: validate`).
- [ ] No generated files hand-edited; run generators when applicable.
- [ ] PR title is imperative and clear; description references handoff ID and purpose.
- [ ] For agent branches, expect Code Owner review on merge into `main`.

# Docs Review — Operating Model

**Objective:** keep documentation accurate as the system evolves.

## Cadence
- **Weekly**: plan-only report of stale docs (based on `last_validated` > 90 days or broken links).
- **On PRs**: Docs CI validates front-matter and links.

## Roles
- **Maintainer**: reviews agent PRs into `main`.
- **Agents**: propose changes via Handoff Runner; update or create docs/templates.

## Signals of staleness
- `last_validated` > 90 days.
- Broken relative links.
- References to retired components (flagged in registry).

## Next step
- Script: `tooling/scripts/plan_docs_review.py` (added in a follow-up) creates a report issue/PR; agents fix items.

---

# System Lifecycle — Discovery → Research → Decision → Project → Implementation → Test → Release → Operate

## 1) Discovery (Problem framing)
- Capture **User Stories** (see template) and success criteria.

## 2) Research
- Use **Research Brief**; agents gather options + tradeoffs + citations.

## 3) Decision
- Record outcome with **Decision Record (ADR-lite)**.

## 4) Project Definition
- Use **Implementation Plan** (apps, services, keys, permissions, sandboxes).

## 5) Implementation & Test
- Build in branch/sandbox; follow **Test Plan**.

## 6) Release & Operate
- Use **Release Checklist**; update registries and docs.
